summary: Specifies how GSMP packets are encapsulated in ATM, Ethernet and TCP. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: The GSMP messages need envelopes for different delivery routes. This defines three.

questions: how is gsmp carried over tcp
subtitle: How General Switch Management Protocol messages are wrapped for ATM, Ethernet and TCP links.

tldr.problem: GSMP messages, which a controller uses to manage a switch, need to be carried over different kinds of links.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three wrappers: ATM AAL-5 with an LLC/SNAP header, Ethernet frames with Ethertype 0x880C plus sender and receiver instance fields, and TCP on port 6068 with a 4-byte type and length header.
tldr.outcome: Any GSMP use over an IP network MUST use the TCP encapsulation, protected by IPsec ESP for integrity and confidentiality.

today: RFC 3293 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It defines encapsulations for the messages specified in RFC 3292.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: GSMP (General Switch Management Protocol) messages are defined in RFC 3292 and MAY be carried over several different protocols. This memo specifies three ways: ATM AAL-5, Ethernet and TCP. It notes that other encapsulations may be defined in future specifications.
sections.eli5: GSMP is how a boss computer talks to a switch. This RFC explains the envelopes used to send those talks.

sections.title: ATM Encapsulation
sections.content:
On an ATM link, GSMP packets are variable length and go directly into an AAL-5 CPCS-PDU with an LLC/SNAP header. That header holds the bytes 0xAA 0xAA 0x03 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x88 0x0C, where 0x880C is the assigned Ethertype for GSMP. After the message comes padding of 0 to 47 bytes and the 8-byte AAL-5 CPCS-PDU trailer.

The MTU of the GSMP Message field is 1492 bytes. The virtual channel carrying a GSMP session between a controller and its switch is the GSMP control channel. Its default is VPI 0 and VCI 15, and it MAY be changed using the GSMP MIB.
sections.eli5: On ATM links the message goes in a special sleeve with a label saying it is GSMP, and the default lane for it is number 15.

sections.title: Ethernet Encapsulation
sections.content:
On Ethernet, a frame carries a Destination Address, Source Address, Ethertype 0x880C, the GSMP message, then Sender Instance, Receiver Instance, Pad and the Frame Check Sequence. The two instance numbers come from the adjacency protocol and are appended to all non-adjacency GSMP messages to give extra protection against corrupt state being introduced.

For the SYN message of the adjacency protocol the destination is the broadcast address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF, or alternatively a configured unicast 48-bit IEEE MAC address. All other messages use the unicast MAC address of the destination, learned from the Source Address of messages received while synchronising. The source is always the sender's 48-bit MAC address. The Pad should be zero bytes so the data field reaches the 46-byte minimum, and is not part of the GSMP message.

Once the adjacency protocol is synchronised, a receiver must discard a message if the Sender Instance and Source Address do not match those stored by the Update Peer Verifier operation, if it arrives on a different port from the one used to synchronise, or if the Receiver Instance does not match the current Sender Instance of the adjacency protocol.
sections.eli5: On Ethernet, each message carries two small ID tags. The receiver checks them and throws away anything that does not match, like a guard checking name badges.

sections.title: TCP/IP Encapsulation
sections.content:
When GSMP is carried over an IP network, it MUST use the TCP encapsulation, because TCP gives reliable transport and flow control suited to networks with high loss and variable delay. The controller runs the client code and the switch runs the server code. The switch listens on TCP port 6068 and MUST be a multi-connection server so several controller instances can each open a control session.

After the TCP connection is up, the controller sends adjacency protocol messages to synchronise with the switch. Other GSMP messages MUST NOT be sent until adjacency has synchronised.

Because TCP is a byte stream, a 4-byte TLV header is prepended to each GSMP message to mark its boundaries. Type is 2 bytes with value 0x880C. Length is a 2-byte unsigned integer giving the length of the GSMP message only, not the 4-byte header. A message is processed only after it is fully received.
sections.eli5: TCP is like a long pipe with no breaks, so each message gets a little note on the front saying how long it is.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
When GSMPv3 is used in IP networks, security between controller and client MUST be available and MUST be provided by IP Security. The IPsec Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) MUST be used for both integrity and confidentiality. For all uses over an IP network, running GSMP over TCP/IP with this protection is REQUIRED.

With ATM and Ethernet encapsulations, security MAY be provided at the link layer, and the RFC leaves those methods out of scope. For secure operation over any media, the IP encapsulation with IPsec SHOULD be used.
sections.eli5: If the messages travel over the internet, they must be locked in a sealed, tamper-proof box so no one can read or change them.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Type code of the following message, the same as GSMP's Ethertype.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Total length of the GSMP message only, not including the 4-byte header.

cells: Required for IP networks; IPsec ESP
